securityReview.method: Static review of the enforcement seam, the route manifest, middleware ordering, the telemetry call sites and the denial path. NO suite was executed in the recording pass: a concurrent './smackerel.sh test e2e' lane was running and a prior concurrent Docker lane had already caused an OOM (exit 137), so every claim below is a code fact confirmed by reading a cited file, never an inferred test result.
cleanConfirmations: OBSERVE is STRUCTURALLY incapable of denying. The observe path's record function takes no http.ResponseWriter, so it has no mechanism with which to write a refusal. The property is enforced by the type signature rather than by a branch that a later edit could invert - the strongest available shape for this guarantee.

Telemetry is strictly DOWNSTREAM of the authorization decision. The allowed counter increments at internal/api/corpus_grant_gate.go:115 only after auth.GateGlobalCorpusRead(sess).Allowed at :114 has already decided, so no metric - including the new bypass counter - can influence who is admitted or refused. This is also what makes the coverage-label rollback analytically safe.

Middleware ordering resolves bearerAuth -> RequireScope -> Observe, and this was verified against chi v5.2.2's ACTUAL With/Group semantics rather than assumed from source reading order. Source order and execution order diverge in chi under Group, so assuming would have been unsound.

No wildcard or empty claim escalates. Session.Scopes is NEVER set to a wildcard sentinel (internal/auth/verify.go:56 states this as a contract), and an absent scope claim yields nil rather than a permissive default - so a token cannot gain authority by omitting the claim.

Bridge delegation cannot confer a grant the principal lacks. deriveGrants NARROWS the mapped principal's persisted set and has no widening path, so the bridge is incapable of minting authority that its principal does not already hold.

TP-03-07's denial byte-identity GENERALISES to all sixteen route groups BY CONSTRUCTION, not by sixteen separate assertions. There is exactly ONE denial site, and its body is a function of the required scope alone, so a per-group divergence is not expressible in the current code. The single-group test is therefore sufficient rather than a sampled shortcut.
correctionsToPriorClaims: A malformed scope claim does NOT drop the bad element and keep the good half - the OPPOSITE of what a previous brief asserted. internal/auth/verify.go getScopeClaim returns (nil, ErrScopeClaimMalformed) the moment ANY element fails ScopeNameRegex (:106-110), and the caller sets scopes = nil (:266-271) while logging a warning. The WHOLE set fails closed, which is the safer shape: a forged or partially-corrupt claim degrades to legacy/no-scopes rather than retaining whichever elements happened to parse.

The design claim that the gate 'answers WHO, never WHAT' is true of the gate's OWN denial log line only. At system level structuredLogger already logs the concrete request path at INFO for every request, so the artifact identifier is in the log regardless. Any statement that no artifact id reaches logs is FALSE AS WRITTEN and needs narrowing wherever it appears; tracked as the second half of SEC-108-04's remedy.

outstandingFindings.summary: A SECOND, ungated corpus surface exists outside the sixteen-group route manifest: four server-rendered HTMX routes read the corpus server-side and the gate never sees them in either stage.
outstandingFindings.detail: POST /search, GET /artifact/{id}, GET /digest and GET /knowledge/concepts/{id} are mounted at ROOT under deps.webAuthMiddleware (internal/api/router.go:480-524), NOT inside the gated group (which sits under the /api prefix at router.go:141-145 wrapped in corpusGate.Observe). They READ THE CORPUS server-side - SearchResults calls the executor and ArtifactDetail queries the artifacts table directly against h.Pool - so they are not API clients of the gated group and the gate observes them in NEITHER stage. Exposure today is bounded to the shared-token band, which auth.RequireScope already bypasses BY DESIGN, so this is NOT an escalation beyond the documented bypass and NOT a live data-exposure defect. It is a LATENT HIGH: spec.md 12 non-goal 5 and F-108-BYPASS-01 both contemplate removing that bypass, and if it is removed the enforcement boundary would LOOK complete while these four families stayed open - the gap would be invisible precisely at the moment it started to matter.
outstandingFindings.validateVerification: Verified by reading, 2026-08-13. Mount split confirmed at internal/api/router.go: the gated corpus groups are registered with corpusGate.Observe(...) under /api (e.g. :141 Get('/digest', deps.DigestHandler), :144-145 Get('/artifact/{id}', deps.ArtifactDetailHandler)), while :482 r.Use(deps.webAuthMiddleware) then :484 r.Post('/search', deps.WebHandler.SearchResults), :485 r.Get('/artifact/{id}', deps.WebHandler.ArtifactDetail), :487 r.Get('/digest', deps.WebHandler.DigestPage), :524 r.Get('/knowledge/concepts/{id}', deps.WebHandler.ConceptDetail) carry no gate. The fixture claim is also TRUE and is recorded IN THE TEST rather than only in the spec: internal/api/router_corpus_gate_test.go:162-179 states the four paths are deliberately absent, that adding them was ATTEMPTED, and that the non-vacuity guard correctly rejected it because corpusGateDeps (:188) leaves Dependencies.WebHandler nil so the whole `if deps.WebHandler != nil` group is unmounted and all four assertions would have been vacuous. outstandingFindings.remedy: Pinning is an INTEGRATION-tier assertion, not a unit one: it needs a real web handler wired into the fixture, and that handler needs a live pool (h.Pool). The documentation half is DONE (design.md 2 + the in-test note); what remains open is the mechanical pin. Clearance bar for a future 'done': either the integration-tier pin exists, or the four families are brought inside the gated manifest, or a recorded adjudication accepts them as permanently out-of-scope with the bypass-removal interaction stated.

outstandingFindings.summary: Web credential login collapses the daily-user band into the bypass band: the session cookie is set to the shared AuthToken, so a browser principal resolves to SessionSourceSharedToken and RequireScope passes it through.
outstandingFindings.detail: internal/api/web_login.go sets the session cookie VALUE to the shared d.AuthToken on successful credential login. That cookie is later accepted as a bearer, resolves to SessionSourceSharedToken, and auth.RequireScope passes it through as a by-design bypass. The consequence FOR THIS SPEC is precise and load-bearing: the daily-user-versus-operator distinction that Scope 04 exists to remediate DOES NOT EXIST for any principal who signs in with username/password - which is exactly the browser population Scope 04 targets. A TP-04-* arm that constructs its fixture via web login is therefore testing the bypass band, not the daily-user band, and would pass whether or not the grant logic works.

The bypass band was therefore invisible in every spec-108 series for the entire observation window, and the per-principal x per-route-group coverage table that gates the ENFORCE flip excluded it not by decision but by construction. Deliberately kept OUT of the would-deny prediction, which is the correct call: a bypassing session is never refused, so counting it there would inflate the UC-108-001 grant list. Bypass band - corpus traffic this coverage table cannot see' (:3316) with its query at :3320, a metric-table row at :2895 and a 'Why the bypass counter exists (SEC-108-03)' rationale at :2898; design.md 4 gained the counter row at :300 and updated the T2 test row at :421 to assert FOUR registered series; spec.md 18 records it at :756 as 'UPDATE 2026-08-13 - a SECOND coverage gap, found by security review (SEC-108-03)'. outstandingFindings.summary: The ENFORCE denial log discloses the principal's FULL grant set, turning the log into a per-principal grant inventory keyed by user_id.
outstandingFindings.detail: internal/auth/scope_middleware.go:90 logs 'token_scopes', sess.Scopes on the denial path. Nothing else in the tree logs Session.Scopes, so this is an INCREMENTAL disclosure rather than a restatement of something already emitted: an operator or anyone with log access can assemble a per-principal grant inventory keyed by user_id from denial traffic alone. The sibling endpoint/path leak is explicitly NOT incremental and should not be conflated with it - structuredLogger already logs the request path at INFO for every request, so the path is in the log regardless of this line.
outstandingFindings.validateVerification: Verified by reading, 2026-08-13. internal/auth/scope_middleware.go:90 carries the literal 'token_scopes', sess.Scopes inside the denial log call (the surrounding bypass increments are at :72 and :76). A tree-wide grep for token_scopes returns exactly this one non-test site, confirming the 'nothing else logs Session.Scopes' half of the claim.
outstandingFindings.remedy: Drop token_scopes from the denial log, or reduce it to len(sess.Scopes) - which preserves the diagnostic signal (did this principal have ANY grants, or none at all?) while removing the inventory. Route to bubbles.plan. SEPARATE and worth recording as a correction rather than folded into the fix: the design claim that the gate 'answers WHO, never WHAT' is true OF THAT ONE LOG LINE ONLY. At system level the concrete request path is already in the request log, so any statement that no artifact id reaches logs is FALSE AS WRITTEN and should be narrowed wherever it appears. Clearance bar for a future 'done': the log line is reduced or dropped, AND the over-broad 'never WHAT' phrasing is corrected.

outstandingFindings.summary: 404-versus-403 reveals which optional subsystems are wired: a CONFIGURATION oracle, not an existence oracle.
outstandingFindings.detail: An ungranted principal receives 403 where the backing subsystem is wired and 404 where it is nil, because the route is only registered when the dependency exists. The distinction is therefore observable from outside. Scope of the leak, stated precisely so it is not over-read: this is a CONFIGURATION oracle - it reveals which optional subsystems this deployment has enabled - and NOT an existence oracle. No artifact identifier, no corpus content, and no per-object existence fact is inferable from it, because the branch is taken on the dependency being nil, never on the requested object.
outstandingFindings.validateVerification: Verified by reading internal/api/router.go, 2026-08-13: :154 `if deps.ContextHandler != nil` and :185 `if deps.IntelligenceEngine != nil` guard route registration, with the comment at :180 recording that the IntelligenceEngine conditional is ENCLOSED by the gated group. The same nil-ness is used deliberately as a vacuity trap in the test fixture (router_corpus_gate_test.go:188, withIntelligence false un-registers all eight Tier B groups), which is what makes the behaviour easy to confirm.
outstandingFindings.remedy: Two proportionate options, and the choice is a planning call rather than an obvious fix. (1) DOCUMENT AND ACCEPT: record the oracle and its bounded scope in the spec, which is proportionate given no object-level fact leaks. (2) Register the Tier-B routes UNCONDITIONALLY behind a 503-when-nil handler, which removes the signal but is a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE and would need its own regression coverage. Route to bubbles.plan. Clearance bar for a future 'done' is an explicit recorded adjudication choosing one - accepting is a valid clearance; leaving it unadjudicated is not.

outstandingFindings.summary: user_id is an unvalidated free-form metric label on the hot allowed path, while the sibling route_group label IS validated against a closed set.
outstandingFindings.detail: RecordCorpusGrantAllowed(group, userID, sessionSource) validates group against the sixteen-value closed set and returns ErrUnknownCorpusRouteGroup on a miss, but userID and sessionSource pass through unvalidated. Since F-108-COVERAGE-LABEL-01 the allowed counter fires on EVERY successful corpus read, so this is now the hot path. The value is bounded TODAY - it is the PASETO sub claim of an enrolled principal, which is minted by the operator - so this is a discipline gap rather than a live cardinality risk. What makes it worth recording is the asymmetry: the guard protecting route_group, whose value set is fixed and cannot grow, is absent on the one label that CAN grow.
outstandingFindings.validateVerification: Verified by reading internal/metrics/auth.go, 2026-08-13: ErrUnknownCorpusRouteGroup is defined at :272 and returned at :288 for the group argument only; RecordCorpusGrantAllowed at :393 takes (group CorpusRouteGroup, userID, sessionSource string) with no validation applied to the latter two.
outstandingFindings.remedy: Either document the bound explicitly (that user_id is the PASETO sub of an operator-enrolled principal, so cardinality is bounded by the roster) or apply a cheap length/charset sanity bound consistent with the route_group precedent. Route to bubbles.plan. Clearance bar for a future 'done' is an explicit recorded adjudication choosing one; documenting the bound is a valid clearance.
